title: Three Weeks and One Short Page
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：introduction　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 introduction 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the editor ① wrote the introduction that no reader in the library would have described, and he said the writing was the whole of the week. The ② introduction, meaning the preface itself and not the page, ran three weeks and stayed undescribed in the book; an introduction, he said, is the only thing in a library that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ introduction in that library had the same short page beside it, and the ④ introduction at the far desk, meaning the chapter they kept for the children to read and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An introduction, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the editor said the describing is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the introduction was the whole of the matter, meaning the guide and not the preface. The ⑥ introduction, meaning the guide and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; introduction, he said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a preface and a guide. He said the guide is the part they remember.

By 1991 the ⑦ introduction had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short page. The ⑧ introduction of the whole thing, the editor wrote in March, was one library and three weeks of describing; introduction, he said, is either the chapter at the far desk or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ introduction I remember is the preface described in the list, which closed in 1993 and is still described as the quietest in the library. An ⑩ introduction, my mother said in 1995, is the only thing that improves by being described; every introduction, she said, is a guide that has agreed to look like a preface. She said the guide was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 介绍；引言（指图书馆里每一篇旁边的那一篇）
B. n. 介绍；引言（指那篇序言本身，与一页相对）
C. 固定搭配：write the introduction 撰写这篇介绍
D. n. 介绍；引言（指留给孩子们读的一章那一篇）
E. n. 导读之事（抽象总称，指一处图书馆的介绍之事）
F. n. 介绍；引言（指目录里写到、被记下的的那一篇）
G. n. 引导、门径（指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 门径（抽象总称，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: wrote the introduction that no reader in the library would have described

the introduction at the far desk

answers.why: write the introduction 意为“撰写这篇介绍”，1986 年那位编辑把图书馆里没有一位读者肯描述的一篇介绍做了一遍。
introduction 意为“介绍；引言”，指那篇序言本身而不是一页，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被描述。
introduction 意为“介绍；引言”，指图书馆里每一篇旁边的那一篇，每一篇旁边都有同一页薄薄的一页。
introduction 意为“介绍；引言”，指最远那张书桌留给孩子们读的一章那一篇，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
introduction 意为“引导、门径”，指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份引导就是那件事的全部。
introduction 意为“门径”，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西而不是那篇序言，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
introduction 意为“介绍；引言”，指目录里写到、被记下的的那一篇，到 1991 年这一篇成了目录里的一行。
introduction 意为“导读之事”，编辑三月写道，整件事的介绍之事是一处图书馆和三个星期的描述。
introduction 意为“介绍；引言”，我记得的是目录里描述过的那一篇，1993 年定稿了，至今仍被说成图书馆里最安静的一篇。
introduction 为抽象总称，母亲 1995 年说，介绍是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的序言。
